subject: Re: Pilot packaging and short-term runway — agile billing vs commit credits
messages:
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@ptx.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Zhou <emily@ptx.ai>
Date: 2025-09-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot runway and billing — quick ask

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the intro call this morning. We made good progress validating the inference latency on a subset of flows, but usage is spikier than we expected. We're near the end of week 3 of our 4-week pilot and the team is asking for a short runway extension to finish a second integration.

Before we commit to a longer-term arrangement, finance is asking for two options we can take back to leadership:
1) a 2-week extension with agile billing (pay-as-you-go during the extension, convert unused spend to a discount if we convert to a contract)
2) a 30-day voucher (prepaid credit) with a small conversion discount if we sign a 12-month committed plan

Can you share which of these you typically support and any standard concession levels? Also attaching our latest token burn export so you can see the spike pattern.

Attachments: ptx_pilot_usage.csv (CSV, 12KB)

Appreciate a quick turnaround — we need to present to the CFO on Thursday.

Best,
Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
CTO, PTX AI
rajiv@ptx.ai
+1 415-555-0183
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@ptx.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway and billing — quick ask

Thanks Rajiv — got the CSV and the signal is clear. Looping in Marissa (sales leader) for approval on concession approach and David (finance) for the conversion mechanics.

Short answer: we can support both options. A couple notes up front so you have context for the CFO slide: 
- 2-week extension (agile billing): we run the same pilot configuration, you continue on pay-as-you-go for that period. If you convert to a committed plan within 30 days of the extension end, we credit a portion of extension spend as a one-time conversion discount. Typical credit is 30–50% of extension spend depending on committed ARR and customer size.
- 30-day voucher (prepay): we can offer a prepaid voucher at a modest discount (typically 10–20%) that applies to platform consumption. Upon conversion, we can increase that to a conversion credit at a higher effective level if you sign a 12-month commit.

Constraints: credits only apply if there is a signed commitment (SOW or Order Form) within the stated window; we cannot retroactively apply credits to previously invoiced public SaaS usage beyond the published conversion window.

Marissa / David — any high-level guardrails you'd add for a pilot this size? Rajiv, based on the CSV it looks like you had two high-burn days (2025-08-27 and 2025-08-30) driven by large batch runs — if you want, our engineering ops team can add a short burst cap to smooth billing for the extension.

Next steps: Marissa / David, can you confirm a recommended credit band and whether we should propose the burst cap? Rajiv, if you can confirm which option you prefer today, I'll draft the short amendment and attach a DocuSign link so CFO can sign before Thursday.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.ai
---
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-09-02T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway and billing — quick ask

On Tue, Sep 1, 2025 at 11:04 AM Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Rajiv — got the CSV and the signal is clear. Looping in Marissa (sales leader) for approval on concession approach and David (finance) for the conversion mechanics.
> 
> Short answer: we can support both options. A couple notes up front so you have context for the CFO slide: 
> - 2-week extension (agile billing): we run the same pilot configuration, you continue on pay-as-you-go for that period. If you convert to a committed plan within 30 days of the extension end, we credit a portion of extension spend as a one-time conversion discount. Typical credit is 30–50% of extension spend depending on committed ARR and customer size.
> - 30-day voucher (prepay): we can offer a prepaid voucher at a modest discount (typically 10–20%) that applies to platform consumption. Upon conversion, we can increase that to a conversion credit at a higher effective level if you sign a 12-month commit.

Rajiv — thanks for the data. We should be pragmatic here since this is a four-week pilot and the goal is to close the pilot-to-prod motion if results hold. My recommended, approval-ready offer: 

Option A (recommended): 2-week extension on pay-as-you-go + burst cap + conversion credit = 40% of extension spend credited back if PTX signs >= $120k ARR within 30 days of extension close.

Option B: 30-day prepaid voucher at 15% discount; if PTX converts to a 12-month commitment >= $180k ARR inside 30 days of voucher exhaustion, we top up an additional 20% credit applied to first invoice.

Rationale: Option A keeps spend aligned to actual usage and reduces the CFO's prepayment risk. Option B is cleaner from an operations perspective but requires a stronger upfront commitment from PTX.

David — finance guardrails: we want a clear conversion trigger (signed order form) and a 30-day conversion window. Credit will be applied as a one-time invoice credit to the first committed invoice (not as a recurring discount). Also recommend a one-time SLA uplift (1.5x support response) during the extension for engineering prioritization.

Rajiv — if that looks reasonable, Stephanie will draft the short amendment. If PTX prefers the voucher, we can prepare a simple prepay invoice and an LOI that captures the conversion incentive.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, GTM — Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Rajiv Patel <rajiv@ptx.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhou <emily@ptx.ai>
Date: 2025-09-03T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway and billing — quick ask

Marissa / Stephanie — thank you, this is exactly what we needed for the CFO. PTX prefers Option A (2-week agile extension + burst cap + 40% conversion credit) assuming that the conversion credit band is confirmed in the amendment and the conversion window is 30 days. We'll take the SLA uplift during the extension.

Two asks before you draft: 
1) Can you include a simple usage protection clause that caps any single-day invoiceable spend during the extension to 2x our 95th percentile day from the CSV? (That protects us from accidental batch spikes.)
2) Please attach the amendment as a Draft (Word) and a DocuSign link so our CFO can sign on Thursday.

I'll also send one more cleaned export (smaller file) if you want it — thanks again for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Rajiv
Rajiv Patel
CTO, PTX AI
